design.captureConsequence: A new return reshapes the frontier and may move its patrol toward your next departure.
design.counterplay: Depart from the side away from the frontier patrol and choose a return before entering an opening.
design.lesson: This egg-decoration-inspired outline stays open; walls cannot create a secretly empty sealed chamber.
design.mastery: Use one side opening and one stepped end opening.
design.memorableMoment: An inward enclosure changes which opening is useful on the next outward cut.
design.routeDecision: Leave the central spindle through a side opening, or reach past the segmented oval end?

design.captureConsequence: The chosen enclosure changes the contour around one arm and the next useful return.
design.counterplay: Use the broad L-shaped foundation to change approach; the optional slow pickup is not required.
design.lesson: Practice changing a frontier route before combining it with an outer patrol.
design.mastery: Close from both arms without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A new return draws the frontier patrol around a different side of the L.
design.routeDecision: Extend the short arm to redirect contour pressure, or reach around the long arm for more ground?

design.captureConsequence: A connection changes the next launch angle without automatically filling the other occupied side. Enclosing the hot pocket makes a new approach usable.
design.counterplay: Use the central platform to change direction. The west rail opens the slow-side approach; the east rail offers a return beneath the hot pocket. Keep a real return beyond every bend.
design.lesson: The lower elbow keeps a field keeper on the west approach. Rails close cuts; the elbow wall does not. Read the locked row before choosing which rail to join.
design.mastery: Join all three foundations and neutralize the lethal pocket without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: Two staggered rails stay useful for different reasons after the first long connector leaves both enemy-held sides contested.
design.routeDecision: Connect the west rail for an approach around the elbow, or establish the east rail and neutralize its hot pocket first?

design.captureConsequence: Connecting foundations shortens later escape paths but also changes the patrol route.
design.counterplay: Keep both ends of a short crossing visible. Redirect the frontier away from the chosen return before extending the cut.
design.lesson: Choose a fallback destination before departing; a frontier patrol still threatens the unfinished trail immediately.
design.mastery: Connect both foundations and close a cut with an active impact without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The alternative landing remains reachable when the first approach becomes pressured.
design.routeDecision: Link the upper landing first or leave two separate return destinations while shaping the frontier?

design.captureConsequence: The two relay captures assemble a cross-board reclaimed route without changing any chamber keeper’s domain.
design.counterplay: Use different launch heights around the central spine; avoid treating four chambers as four compulsory identical cuts.
design.lesson: Each occupied chamber remains a separate field problem. A junction opens traversal, not an automatic chamber clear.
design.mastery: Use both opened junctions and clear all required objectives without a life loss.
design.memorableMoment: A formerly blocked side of the central hub becomes a useful return from either adjacent chamber.
design.routeDecision: Use the first opened junction to move through the hub or work around the outside to reach the opposite relay before the frontier approaches?

design.captureConsequence: Closing the pocket can separate keeper regions and reshape patrol pressure at the mouth.
design.counterplay: The mouth stays broad enough for a direct route without collecting the freeze pickup.
design.lesson: Combine distinct outer and frontier patrol routes; the optional freeze never replaces a legal return.
design.mastery: Use an inward and an outward return without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: An open shelter becomes two differently threatened approaches after closure.
design.routeDecision: Close the pocket mouth first or cross outward while the frontier patrol works around the other side?

design.captureConsequence: Each added connection shortens both partners’ routes, but an enclosure can also introduce pressure on that connection.
design.counterplay: The middle wall has two distinct bypasses. Keep the lethal pocket outside cuts until enclosed and avoid funneling both craft into the same active roamer.
design.lesson: Combine known return networks, material decisions and wake-up timing without learning another rule.
design.mastery: Activate both roamers and connect both intermediate islands to the perimeter, with a closure from each craft and no knockdowns.
design.memorableMoment: Four separated islands become a shared network with two moving reclaimed-ground threats.
design.routeDecision: Reach opposite stepping islands first, or connect along one flank and let a partner reopen the other approach?

design.captureConsequence: The western shield extends the central dock with non-scoring return cells; the exposed stage still requires a fresh closure during the opening.
design.counterplay: Capture removes the marked speed effect, so reassess the return trip. Wait on a platform, away from perimeter and frontier patrol paths, before a long release cut.
design.lesson: Known arrows and permanent relays alter route efficiency, not the Sentinel cadence. No new rule is introduced in this optional Remix.
design.mastery: Use the opened release dock and secure a release cut of at least sixteen new cells without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The earlier shortcut becomes the return point for the final ambitious cut.
design.routeDecision: Open the release dock first, or use the marked northern approach to rearrange the frontier before disabling the other shields?

design.captureConsequence: An enclosure neutralizes the bank immediately, but route resilience depends on which foundations you connect.
design.counterplay: Keep the next permanent return in view, repair a valuable gap, and do not treat cooled terrain as permanently protected.
design.lesson: Lanes and erosion use separate warnings. Foundations never erode; reclaimed hazards can reactivate if earned territory reopens.
design.mastery: Neutralize both lethal banks, connect all four foundations and clear without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A permanent alternate return remains available when an earned frontier is marked for erosion.
design.routeDecision: Use an earned shortcut across a cooled bank or connect permanent landings before erosion can reopen that route?

design.captureConsequence: The western shield extends the central dock with non-scoring return cells; the exposed stage still requires a fresh closure during the opening.
design.counterplay: Capture removes the marked speed effect, so reassess the return trip. Wait on a platform, away from perimeter and frontier patrol paths, before a long release cut.
design.lesson: Known arrows and permanent relays alter route efficiency, not the Sentinel cadence. No new rule is introduced in this optional Remix.
design.mastery: Use the opened release dock and secure a release cut of at least sixteen new cells without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The earlier shortcut becomes the return point for the final ambitious cut.
design.routeDecision: Open the release dock first, or use the marked northern approach to rearrange the frontier before disabling the other shields?

design.captureConsequence: Closure cancels the committed attack. The adapted actor still retains its occupied field region, while the existing wall, foundation and patrol rules remain unchanged.
design.counterplay: Inspect both open sides before leaving, keep a contrasting landing in reach, and close while the committed approach still follows its locked route.
design.lesson: The pursuer locks one visible point on the live stitch-like trail; the wall motif blocks sensing but never closes the cut.
design.mastery: Cancel a committed pursuit at each far landing without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A short stitch closure cancels pursuit and turns the next diamond opening into a different route decision.
design.routeDecision: Close at the nearby diamond landing after a pursuit warning, or continue through the stepped opening toward the farther return?

design.captureConsequence: A captured belt loses both its hazard and arrow effect where reclaimed. A line-only connection can still improve the next return without a large reveal.
design.counterplay: The center gaps avoid lethal field. Read both keeper positions before a large enclosure; the separated terraces offer shorter closures and an optional freeze detour.
design.lesson: Combine established terrain neutralization, enemy-retained regions and changing-frontier routes. A marked crossing changes exposure time, not control direction.
design.mastery: Reclaim both lethal side fields completely and visit the connected lower terrace before clearing without a life loss.
design.memorableMoment: A threatening striped belt becomes an ordinary sideways return while the frontier patrol takes its new contour.
design.routeDecision: Cross the open center between the three belts, or enclose a hazardous side belt to create a wider return?

design.captureConsequence: An earned pad connection supplies a departure on another side of the central cluster; occupied field still retains normally.
design.counterplay: Read the field keepers before choosing a point opening. Keep the next pad visible, and use the outside of a satellite cluster if the inner approach is pressured.
design.lesson: The four assembly pads close cuts; the eight-point work-mat obstacles block craft and keepers but never become return surfaces.
design.mastery: Connect all four motor pads using both an inner opening and an outer-cluster approach without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A short diagonal-looking gap demands a deliberate orthogonal route, while the next pad offers an entirely different angle around the star.
design.routeDecision: Connect an adjacent motor pad through an opening between star points, or circle an outer cluster for a larger enclosure and a different return angle?

design.captureConsequence: Link order determines where the surviving keeper regions remain and how long later returns take.
design.counterplay: Watch each keeper before departing; close early when its path threatens the line.
design.lesson: Combine known closure and foundation rules; the finale adds no mandatory mechanic.
design.mastery: Connect all five foundations without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: Five separated foundations become a single useful return network.
design.routeDecision: Connect the nearest outpost, or establish a long return that separates the three keepers?

design.captureConsequence: The short western connection wakes a non-retaining roamer; broader enclosures expand its reclaimed movement domain. The central landing offers a different next return.
design.counterplay: The tracked body marks the western outside route. Prepare another exit, turn along the perimeter after banking, or have your partner connect the middle landing before you return through the changed ground. Baffles are walls, never returns.
design.lesson: A quick return can become a shared patrol route. The full one-second wake warning gives time to choose a fresh departure.
design.mastery: Activate the roamer before clearing, with a closure from each craft and no knockdowns.
design.memorableMoment: The line that rescued one craft becomes a moving threat while a partner opens a second approach.
design.routeDecision: Take the short outside return and wake its roamer, or connect toward the middle landing before opening that escape?

design.captureConsequence: Connecting the circuit reshapes both field and reclaimed-ground danger without changing the capture contract.
design.counterplay: Watch the enemy trail strike and the current patrol route; close early enough to preserve an exit from a newly awakened roamer.
design.lesson: Combine known impact, frontier and reclaimed-ground rules. This optional Remix adds no mandatory mechanic.
design.mastery: Close a cut with an active impact after the roamer activates and neutralize the lethal bank without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: An impact is extinguished at the return just as a new escape corridor becomes necessary.
design.routeDecision: Keep disconnected fallback landings or connect a circuit that gives both the craft and frontier patrol new routes?

design.captureConsequence: Capturing a new inner return does not redirect the outer patrol.
design.counterplay: The first island offers an interior return while the patrol stays on the outside rail.
design.lesson: Reclaimed ground closes a cut, but the outer patrol can still hit the craft there.
design.mastery: Complete without touching the outer patrol.
design.memorableMoment: A return inside the board avoids a dangerous stretch of the outer rail.
design.routeDecision: Leave before the outer patrol approaches, or wait for it to pass and return behind it?

design.captureConsequence: Link order determines where the surviving keeper regions remain and how long later returns take.
design.counterplay: Watch each keeper before departing; close early when its path threatens the line.
design.lesson: Combine known closure and foundation rules; the finale adds no mandatory mechanic.
design.mastery: Connect all five foundations without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: Five separated foundations become a single useful return network.
design.routeDecision: Connect the nearest outpost, or establish a long return that separates the three keepers?

design.captureConsequence: A bridge between lanes creates a new return and can move the contour across the next intended approach.
design.counterplay: The upper and lower gaps stay wide; wait on a foundation and choose the side away from patrol pressure.
design.lesson: Staggered return lanes reward planning the next departure, not just reaching the nearest reclaimed cell.
design.mastery: Join all three return lanes without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: One diagonal-looking route is executed as clear orthogonal cuts between staggered platforms.
design.routeDecision: Alternate the broad top and bottom connections, or take a slow central link to reshape the frontier sooner?

design.captureConsequence: A partner-built bridge creates a new bank and launch point; the quick outside closure instead wakes reclaimed-ground pressure along the shared route.
design.counterplay: Coordinate the Interceptor around the active cut and the Disruptor around moving field pressure. Build the middle connection before waking the outside roamer so the partner has another return.
design.lesson: The Interceptor protects the longer exposed connection while the Disruptor controls the keeper window. A return earned by either craft becomes shared ground for both.
design.mastery: Activate the roamer before clearing, with a closure from each craft and no knockdowns.
design.memorableMoment: The line that rescued one craft becomes a moving threat while a partner opens a second approach.
design.routeDecision: Take the short outside return and wake its roamer, or connect toward the middle landing before opening that escape?

design.captureConsequence: An earned passage connection creates a return beside the next bend. It does not turn the wall into reclaimed ground or move the perimeter patrol onto the new frontier.
design.counterplay: Watch the keeper between the bands before crossing the open weave. Use a return beyond one band end if the inner passage is pressured, and avoid waiting in the outer patrol path.
design.lesson: Inspect the wall immediately below the starting reclaimed pad. The zigzag bands block movement and cannot close a cut; the small return pads stop before the gaps rather than bridging them for free.
design.mastery: Make one closure through an inner gap and another around a band end without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A route that turns right around the first embroidered band must reconsider its approach at the left-facing second band.
design.routeDecision: Connect the short upper landing and weave through the alternating inner gaps, or wrap a band end for a broader enclosure while timing the perimeter patrol?

design.captureConsequence: Enclosing the roamer changes reclaimed-ground pressure; the carrier and keeper retain field normally.
design.counterplay: Keep broad cross-connections available. A permanent landing closes the cut but does not protect against an active roamer.
design.lesson: A capture can remove terrain danger and wake a different movement-domain threat at the same time.
design.mastery: Neutralize both lethal banks and close a cut after the roamer activates without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A blocked-looking approach becomes clear, then requires a different return plan as the roamer wakes.
design.routeDecision: Open the northern clear channel or the southern island connection while preserving room for the reclaimed-ground roamer?

design.captureConsequence: The first capture chooses which outer route becomes ordinary ground and reshapes patrol pressure.
design.counterplay: Depart through the clear center, preserving multiple returns while watching both patrol domains.
design.lesson: Slow and lethal marks have different consequences; both are neutralized by capture.
design.mastery: Neutralize both beds without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A reclaimed central cross makes the same board approachable from four directions.
design.routeDecision: Open the slower west approach first or enclose the lethal east bed while keeping the central return?

design.captureConsequence: The first captured area becomes the return surface for a shorter second cut.
design.counterplay: Watch each keeper before departing; close early when its path threatens the line.
design.lesson: A hit on an unfinished line sends visible impacts along it. Reach reclaimed ground before the craft-bound front arrives.
design.mastery: Complete the mission in three cuts or fewer.
design.memorableMoment: A cautious first cut changes the best route for the next one.
design.routeDecision: Take the nearby narrow slice now, or travel along the rail for a larger enclosure?

design.captureConsequence: Linking rows changes the frontier and the reclaimed movement domain in different ways.
design.counterplay: The near landing starts away from both threats; watch the middle lane before connecting it.
design.lesson: A foundation can already support a warned roamer; its interior route differs from the patrol tracing the field edge.
design.mastery: Join all three rows and neutralize the slow link without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: Two enemies use different parts of the same newly connected return network.
design.routeDecision: Take the clear long link around the middle roamer, or neutralize the slow gap to make a shorter next departure?

design.captureConsequence: Linking rows changes the frontier and the reclaimed movement domain in different ways.
design.counterplay: The near landing starts away from both threats; watch the middle lane before connecting it.
design.lesson: A foundation can already support a warned roamer; its interior route differs from the patrol tracing the field edge.
design.mastery: Join all three rows and neutralize the slow link without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: Two enemies use different parts of the same newly connected return network.
design.routeDecision: Take the clear long link around the middle roamer, or neutralize the slow gap to make a shorter next departure?

design.captureConsequence: Connecting either side of the middle platform creates a new bank; the partner can use it to replace the long outer return with a shorter second approach.
design.counterplay: Use Disruptor Support before committing around a wall tip, then Interceptor Support for the partner’s longer exposed crossing. Approach the platform from opposite ends instead of duplicating one route.
design.lesson: One specialist establishes the winding approach while the other protects the crossing that turns the middle platform into shared ground.
design.mastery: Both craft visit the centre platform after it is connected to the perimeter and each closes a cut, without knockdowns.
design.memorableMoment: Both craft arrive at one middle platform from opposite ends of the switchback.
design.routeDecision: Bank the outer pockets first, or approach the shared middle platform from opposite wall tips?

design.captureConsequence: Anchor order changes which established connections can be relied upon during later captures.
design.counterplay: Use broad cross arms to change departure direction and avoid following the frontier patrol into a narrow return.
design.lesson: Two captured anchors can protect different connections; five foundations are return choices, not five mandatory chores.
design.mastery: Capture both anchors before reaching three quarters of the earned target, without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: Two protected routes support a larger capture without requiring every island to be visited.
design.routeDecision: Bank the western connection first, or secure the eastern anchor while keeping a cross-shaped landing between both eroders?

design.captureConsequence: An approach capture creates useful return ground without automatically defeating the core. The same exposed-stage release rule applies.
design.counterplay: The walls block turns and never close cuts. The frontier follows your new return edge; the roamer activates on reclaimed ground.
design.lesson: Deep receiver galleries share the Sentinel field. Choose returns outside the baffles before committing to an inner cut.
design.mastery: Capture the lower receiver before the upper receiver, in separate closures, and clear without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The second receiver approach becomes visible beyond the first gallery wall.
design.routeDecision: Secure the upper gallery approach first, or the lower landing, before turning around a receiver baffle?

design.captureConsequence: Connecting the circuit reshapes both field and reclaimed-ground danger without changing the capture contract.
design.counterplay: Watch the carrier’s trail strike and the current patrol route; close early enough to preserve an exit from a newly awakened roamer.
design.lesson: Combine known impact, frontier and reclaimed-ground rules. This optional Remix adds no mandatory mechanic.
design.mastery: Close a cut with an active impact after the roamer activates and neutralize the lethal bank without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: An impact is extinguished at the return just as a new escape corridor becomes necessary.
design.routeDecision: Keep disconnected fallback landings or connect a circuit that gives both the craft and frontier patrol new routes?

design.captureConsequence: Each added connection shortens both partners’ routes, but an enclosure can also introduce pressure on that connection.
design.counterplay: The middle wall has two distinct bypasses. Keep the lethal pocket outside cuts until enclosed and avoid funneling both craft into the same active roamer.
design.lesson: Combine known return networks, material decisions and wake-up timing without learning another rule.
design.mastery: Activate both roamers and connect both intermediate islands to the perimeter, with a closure from each craft and no knockdowns.
design.memorableMoment: Four separated islands become a shared network with two moving reclaimed-ground threats.
design.routeDecision: Reach opposite stepping islands first, or connect along one flank and let a partner reopen the other approach?

design.captureConsequence: Neutralizing terrain and protecting a return connection solve different parts of the same route.
design.counterplay: Keep the middle reserve and choose an approach outside the active roamer’s reclaimed domain.
design.lesson: Capture order should make the next route easier, not demand that every repeated cluster be cleared.
design.mastery: Neutralize both marked terrain areas and capture both anchors without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: An awkward stagger becomes a useful diagonal sequence of axis-aligned captures.
design.routeDecision: Secure the slowing northern connection first, or enclose the southern danger pocket before banking its anchor?

design.captureConsequence: A captured belt loses both its hazard and arrow effect where reclaimed. A line-only connection can still improve the next return without a large reveal.
design.counterplay: The center gaps avoid lethal field. Read both keeper positions before a large enclosure; the separated terraces offer shorter closures and an optional freeze detour.
design.lesson: Combine established terrain neutralization, enemy-retained regions and changing-frontier routes. A marked crossing changes exposure time, not control direction.
design.mastery: Reclaim both lethal side fields completely and visit the connected lower terrace before clearing without a life loss.
design.memorableMoment: A threatening striped belt becomes an ordinary sideways return while the frontier patrol takes its new contour.
design.routeDecision: Cross the open center between the three belts, or enclose a hazardous side belt to create a wider return?

design.captureConsequence: A reclaimed neck removes its speed penalty and changes the value of the next central crossing.
design.counterplay: Compare the keeper positions with both nearby landings. Cross an arrow band at right angles when its direction is unhelpful.
design.lesson: Shortest distance and shortest exposure need not be the same. Across an arrow is ordinary speed, not a sideways push.
design.mastery: Reclaim both central necks and clear without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: An initially awkward against-arrow route becomes the best ordinary-speed connection after capture.
design.routeDecision: Use the short central neck against the lower arrows or take the longer lateral approach with them?

design.captureConsequence: The same step is a useful short closure before activation and a place to keep moving afterward.
design.counterplay: Leave both ends of the stepped platform usable and depart again when the roamer approaches.
design.lesson: A return closes the trail but does not protect the craft from an active roamer approaching along reclaimed ground.
design.mastery: Use both ends of the stepped foundation for closures after activating the roamer.
design.memorableMoment: A familiar return surface becomes a timing choice without changing the capture rule.
design.routeDecision: Return to the short upper step or the long lower arm while the warned roamer patrols the stepped foundation?

design.captureConsequence: Opposite captures can build a shared central corridor. A line-only closure still supplies a return route while occupied regions stay unclaimed.
design.counterplay: The west spine offers several returns; the east refuge has clear upper and lower bypasses. Watch both keepers before a long vertical cut.
design.lesson: A partner can neutralize material for both craft; the lethal bed must be enclosed before either craft crosses it.
design.mastery: Neutralize both material beds with a closure from each craft and no knockdowns.
design.memorableMoment: One partner opens the marked crossing while the other turns a slow approach into ordinary shared ground.
design.routeDecision: Split the outer bypasses to enclose both material beds, or first link a shared return through the slow approach?

design.captureConsequence: A chamber clear can move its main danger onto the shared perimeter without completing the other chamber.
design.counterplay: Keep a perimeter connection in each chamber. The divider blocks movement and cannot close a cut; use Support if a roamer approaches a return.
design.lesson: Each occupied chamber keeps its own field, while each reclaimed roamer changes the local return route.
design.mastery: Activate both roamers, with each craft closing in its starting chamber and no knockdowns.
design.memorableMoment: Two independent wake-up decisions meet on a common perimeter.
design.routeDecision: Wake the depot roamers together, or let one partner secure a return while the other changes their chamber?

design.captureConsequence: A landing connection improves your next escape without clearing the other occupied bay. Neither bay alone reaches the coverage target.
design.counterplay: The northern landing offers a short return. Watch the bolt before extending your trail; close before its impact reaches you. Use the center deck to change bays, and never mistake a wall for a return.
design.lesson: Only the bolt carrier sends travelling impacts. The two lower keepers break a trail immediately; each occupied bay retains its own field.
design.mastery: Close a cut with an active travelling impact without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A small landing return extinguishes an impact; the lower bay then asks for a different enclosure around its baffles.
design.routeDecision: Practice a short northern landing return, or work around the lower baffles for a larger enclosure between two keepers?

design.captureConsequence: Closure cancels the committed attack. The adapted actor still retains its occupied field region, while the existing wall, foundation and patrol rules remain unchanged.
design.counterplay: Depart behind the outer patrol, use an inner return strip to cancel pursuit, and keep the next alternating passage open.
design.lesson: Alternating rushnyk-inspired openings change which side offers cover; pursuit and the outer patrol pressure different parts of the route.
design.mastery: Cancel pursuit through both inner passages without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A left-to-right escape cancels pursuit, then the mirrored band demands the opposite approach.
design.routeDecision: Cross through the nearer alternating band before pursuit commits, or circle the end while preserving an inner strip as the fallback return?

design.captureConsequence: Reconnecting the spine creates a useful route that both active roamers may also use.
design.counterplay: Use broad gaps and distinct upper/lower returns, neutralize marked pockets by enclosure and leave a fresh departure ready.
design.lesson: Combine known retention, return-ground, terrain and threat-domain rules; no new mandatory mechanic.
design.mastery: Join the three spine segments and activate both roamers without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: An apparently broken return network becomes useful only after choosing how to keep it escapable.
design.routeDecision: Reconnect the broken spine, or first establish a vertical escape before the two sleepers gain access to it?

design.captureConsequence: Each captured trigger removes a different return detour; opening never performs a second hidden flood.
design.counterplay: Read the inner keeper before a short closure and keep the broad lower opening as an alternative to the gated route.
design.lesson: The field keeper, not a closed gate, retains each chamber. Numbered links change player routes without moving that keeper into another region.
design.mastery: Open the lower connector first and clear without a life loss.
design.memorableMoment: The inner link opens while the neighbouring keeper remains in exactly the same field component.
design.routeDecision: Open the cross-ring link before taking the inner trigger, or use the open lower approach and preserve the shorter return for later?

design.captureConsequence: Both chambers contribute to the same coverage quota. Neither half alone can supply the required clear.
design.counterplay: The divider blocks movement and never banks a trail. Return to an island or the perimeter; each chamber has a visible keeper.
design.lesson: Each occupied chamber needs its own useful capture; closing one side does not clear the other.
design.mastery: Each craft closes in its starting chamber and connects its island to the perimeter without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: Two independent enclosures transform opposite halves of one board.
design.routeDecision: Work opposite chambers in parallel, or travel around the perimeter to help the pressured partner?

design.captureConsequence: Each connection changes the next usable return and the patrol contour.
design.counterplay: Use the clear sides of the rungs and observe the frontier before returning. The slow lower approach is optional, not a forced precision sprint.
design.lesson: A sequence of deliberate returns can reduce impact exposure more than a single ambitious crossing.
design.mastery: Connect all three foundations and close a cut with an active impact without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The ladder acquires a new rung through the player’s own capture.
design.routeDecision: Build short diagonal connections between staggered landings, or expose a longer trail to reclaim a larger side?

design.captureConsequence: Capturing a spoke creates a permanent-speed return while the frontier moves around the newly reclaimed edge.
design.counterplay: Turn on the central platform first and watch the frontier before making a second connection. Open corners provide unmarked alternatives.
design.lesson: Changing the frontier changes patrol routes, but never rotates arrows or alters their strength.
design.mastery: Connect three outer windbreaks and clear without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: Four visibly different approaches converge on one platform without forced spinning or drift.
design.routeDecision: Follow one spoke to a broad windbreak or cross between spokes to shape a shorter frontier?

design.captureConsequence: Connection order changes the fastest return route and which marked channel can be neutralized next.
design.counterplay: The upper and lower clear approaches remain available; the freeze detour is optional.
design.lesson: Combine known terrain and patrol rules; no new mandatory mechanic is introduced.
design.mastery: Link all three refuges without collecting the optional freeze.
design.memorableMoment: Three separated refuges become a route network through two distinct kinds of field.
design.routeDecision: Link the near and central refuges through slow ground, or loop around the marked channel to the far landing?

design.captureConsequence: The growing network changes field and reclaimed-ground threat domains in different ways.
design.counterplay: The permanent hub cannot erode but can still host a roamer; preserve a fresh departure and do not confuse permanence with immunity from enemies.
design.lesson: Combine known erosion, anchor, roamer and frontier rules. No new mandatory mechanic.
design.mastery: Capture both anchors, make a repair and close a cut after the hub roamer activates, without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A damaged network still offers a deliberate escape because its essential connections were banked.
design.routeDecision: Bank two useful connections while routing around reclaimed-ground pressure, or take a larger capture while leaving a reserve return?

design.captureConsequence: Capturing a spoke creates a permanent-speed return while the frontier moves around the newly reclaimed edge.
design.counterplay: Turn on the central platform first and watch the frontier before making a second connection. Open corners provide unmarked alternatives.
design.lesson: Changing the frontier changes patrol routes, but never rotates arrows or alters their strength.
design.mastery: Connect three outer windbreaks and clear without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: Four visibly different approaches converge on one platform without forced spinning or drift.
design.routeDecision: Follow one spoke to a broad windbreak or cross between spokes to shape a shorter frontier?

design.captureConsequence: Clearing one chamber contributes shared coverage and frees that pilot to support the other chamber; it never silently clears the occupied field across the divider.
design.counterplay: Use Disruptor Support to create the keeper window in the active chamber and Interceptor Support to protect its longer exposed cut. After banking, travel the perimeter rather than treating the divider as a return.
design.lesson: Each specialist secures a different occupied chamber, then can redeploy around the shared perimeter to protect the partner’s remaining closure.
design.mastery: Each craft closes in its starting chamber and connects its island to the perimeter without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: Two independent enclosures transform opposite halves of one board.
design.routeDecision: Work opposite chambers in parallel, or travel around the perimeter to help the pressured partner?

design.captureConsequence: Capturing one row opens route choices without requiring the second row to be crossed.
design.counterplay: Use the broad upper and lower bypasses, then return to a foundation or earned ground.
design.lesson: Clear lanes between lethal rows are still unclaimed field, not guaranteed return ground.
design.mastery: Neutralize at least one marked row and connect both refuges without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A long protected spine offers several departures into the same changing hazard problem.
design.routeDecision: Neutralize the nearer row from the spine, or loop around the ends to reach the far refuge first?

design.captureConsequence: Connecting a lens pad reshapes the patrol contour on that side without clearing the other keeper’s occupied field.
design.counterplay: Depart away from the frontier patrol. Read the keeper inside the chosen approach and keep the opposite lens pad available before extending around a shoulder.
design.lesson: The opposing work-mat panels block movement but remain open field problems. Lens pads close cuts; keeper positions decide what fills.
design.mastery: Make a closure from each lens pad, using a facing opening and an exterior shoulder without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The eastern landing needs a dogleg around a detached shoulder after the direct western connection.
design.routeDecision: Take the direct western lens approach, or bend above or below the eastern panel shoulder before returning to its landing?

design.captureConsequence: A closure changes the contour that the patrol follows; it does not become a field-retaining enemy.
design.counterplay: The first return approaches the broad top of the island, away from the patrol on its left edge.
design.lesson: Unlike the outer patrol, a frontier patrol follows the changing field/reclaimed boundary.
design.mastery: Create a new frontier and depart from a different edge.
design.memorableMoment: The newly reclaimed edge becomes part of the patrol route.
design.routeDecision: Close ahead of the moving frontier patrol, or shape a return on the opposite side of its route?

design.captureConsequence: A capture changes your return options but can create an eligible frontier for erosion.
design.counterplay: Watch the eroder stop and mark a cell. Keep a permanent return within reach instead of chasing every lost cell.
design.lesson: The marked cell warns before reopening. Foundations remain permanent; earned ground can need repair.
design.mastery: Repair an eroded cell with a legal closure without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A small gap reopens beside a landing that stays intact.
design.routeDecision: Use the permanent landing for repeated returns, or bank a larger exposed edge that the eroder can reopen?

design.captureConsequence: Capture order determines which branch remains a convenient return under pressure.
design.counterplay: Use the broad central branch to switch sides; leave another return available before enlarging the roamer’s domain.
design.lesson: An escape corridor needs a usable departure, not merely a connection to reclaimed cells occupied by a roamer.
design.mastery: Connect both outer platforms and neutralize the marked pocket without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The best next capture opens a way out rather than maximizing immediate area.
design.routeDecision: Build an outside escape to the near platform, or neutralize the marked pocket before joining the far platform?

design.captureConsequence: An inner landing shortens a later cut without banking against a wall. Outer returns introduce reclaimed-ground pressure, and two retainers keep each chamber contested until deliberately enclosed.
design.counterplay: The top and bottom baffle ends stay open. Watch both local keepers before crossing; after waking a roamer, turn onto a different return rather than waiting on its new rail. Either partner may travel around the divider to help. Coordinate the Interceptor around exposed lines and the Disruptor around moving threats; neither pulse substitutes for the other.
design.lesson: Interceptor Support removes nearby travelling impacts while Disruptor Support slows nearby enemies. Rescue remains available to both players.
design.mastery: Activate both roamers, with each craft closing in its starting chamber and no knockdowns.
design.memorableMoment: A quick outside escape and a protected inner receiver become two different ways to reopen the same depot.
design.routeDecision: Wake the outer return patrols for quick perimeter access, or wrap the inner baffles to establish receiver landings first?

design.captureConsequence: An outer enclosure can remove a garden and an approach together, giving the other craft a full-speed return.
design.counterplay: Keep the lethal gardens outside your route until they are reclaimed. Time the central keeper before attempting a shared bridge.
design.lesson: A short route through slow field can keep a trail exposed longer than an outer bypass.
design.mastery: Neutralize every slow and lethal patch with a closure from each craft and no knockdowns.
design.memorableMoment: Two dangerous gardens become ordinary shared ground around a contested middle island.
design.routeDecision: Link through a slow approach to reach the middle island, or split the outer routes and clear the gardens first?

design.captureConsequence: A connection can send frontier pressure around one frame while the other remains open.
design.counterplay: Leave the bridge away from the frontier patrol and preserve the opposite side as a return option.
design.lesson: Open frames are not separate capture rules: only keeper positions decide retained regions.
design.mastery: Make a closure from each lens landing.
design.memorableMoment: One shared bridge supports two different chamber problems.
design.routeDecision: Work inward toward one lens landing, or close around the outside of both open frames?

design.captureConsequence: Every bridge creates a new possible closure; no route requires a lucky bonus.
design.counterplay: Watch each keeper before departing; close early when its path threatens the line.
design.lesson: Choose a route using both return distance and the future shape of retained regions.
design.mastery: Join the two side outposts without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The final bridge turns separated outposts into a useful loop.
design.routeDecision: Use a top or bottom stepping platform, or attempt the exposed direct bridge?

design.captureConsequence: The upper join leaves a broad lower region; the lower gathered join leaves a different upper region and a closer angle to the east shoulder.
design.counterplay: Use the west shoulder as safe staging, then commit above or below only when the corresponding keeper is travelling away from the intended line.
design.lesson: Offset paired groups around a strong side-to-side joining axis make route planning visible while retaining only known foundation rules.
design.mastery: Reach both offset joins from the west shoulder without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A Verkhovyna-informed shoulder construction resolves into two offset joining groups rather than a symmetric cross.
design.routeDecision: Join through the upper shoulder group for the shorter first return, or descend to the offset gathered group for a longer line that approaches the far shoulder?

design.captureConsequence: Relay corners stay permanent while erosion can restore a marked inner spoke. Carrier impacts still disappear when a valid closure secures the trail.
design.counterplay: Enclose the two lethal patches before crossing them. The optional speed pickup sits on a wide straight return, away from mandatory precision turns.
design.lesson: This optional combination uses only known roles. The protected circuit and earned spokes have different erosion consequences; neither changes the capture contract.
design.mastery: Traverse both opened corners and neutralize both lethal patches before clearing without a life loss.
design.memorableMoment: Two missing corners become a complete durable circuit around a changing interior.
design.routeDecision: Complete the protected outer circuit through relay corners, or use the shorter marked center while field threats remain on opposite sides?

design.captureConsequence: New links change route length; the keepers still determine which regions fill.
design.counterplay: Watch each keeper before departing; close early when its path threatens the line.
design.lesson: Connected islands turn one long exposure into several shorter decisions.
design.mastery: Connect all three islands before the clear.
design.memorableMoment: A chain of small connections makes the broad final enclosure possible.
design.routeDecision: Join successive islands for short returns or bypass one for a larger enclosure?

design.captureConsequence: The first reclaimed bed determines which side offers a shorter, faster next route.
design.counterplay: Return to either end of the spine; the optional life is not needed to complete the board.
design.lesson: Reclaimed routes stay fast even when the adjacent unclaimed approach is slow.
design.mastery: Reclaim one entire slow bed before crossing the other.
design.memorableMoment: Two apparently symmetric sides offer different return distances from the interior start.
design.routeDecision: Use the central spine to enclose one slow bed first, or take a larger route around both?

design.captureConsequence: The west closure keeps a compact home return; the eastern stitch creates a smaller but more central departure for the following enclosure.
design.counterplay: Read the western keeper before the short closure. For the eastern join, leave from the upper edge and turn only after the keeper is moving away from the bent trail.
design.lesson: A broad home panel and two broken joining points create different return distances without adding a rule beyond foundations and keeper reads.
design.mastery: Complete both the short western join and the bent eastern join without a loss.
design.memorableMoment: A Vyzhenka-informed broken joining rhythm turns one outpost into a short seam and an offset double return.
design.routeDecision: Close the short western join from the home panel, or make the longer bent return to the offset eastern stitches before choosing the next enclosure?

design.captureConsequence: The opened yards share return ground while their outer field remains governed by the ordinary enemy-retained fill rule.
design.counterplay: Leave a long escape corridor before reclaiming the roamer and use the upper landing as an alternate departure.
design.lesson: An opened connector is permanent, but reclaimed-ground roamers may still use it after activation.
design.mastery: Visit both outer yards after opening their links and clear without a life loss.
design.memorableMoment: A new cross-yard connection becomes both an escape route and possible roamer territory.
design.routeDecision: Connect the western yard first or claim the eastern trigger while keeping a retreat away from the dormant roamer?

design.captureConsequence: A rewarding capture can create both new return ground and a new threat on that ground.
design.counterplay: The first island return wakes the sleeper behind you. Watch its one-second warning, then use either side of the broad platform for your next departure.
design.lesson: A dormant roamer does not retain field. Reclaiming its full body starts a warning, then it moves and threatens reclaimed ground.
design.mastery: Activate the roamer and complete another closure without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: Your first thin connection wakes a threat on the very ground you just reclaimed; the broad landing gives room to choose a way out.
design.routeDecision: Wake the sleeper on the short island connection, or build a side return before reclaiming its corridor?

design.captureConsequence: One closure can clear a travelling impact and open a permanent connection, but the emitter still retains its field.
design.counterplay: Close before the marked lane fires, then use the new connection while preserving space from an activated roamer.
design.lesson: Combine established relay, lane and impact rules. Opening a link changes return choices, not enemy attack periods.
design.mastery: Open a connector on a cut carrying an active impact and clear without a life loss.
design.memorableMoment: An opened link provides a fresh launch point after a narrow closure escapes a known lane attack.
design.routeDecision: Spend the next attack window opening a new escape connection or enclose a smaller region while keeping the roamer dormant?

design.captureConsequence: The growing cross offers shorter return paths; both stationary anchors continue to retain their own regions.
design.counterplay: Choose one short connection at a time. Close before the simultaneous attacks instead of trying to outrun both with a long live trail.
design.lesson: Two known emitters mark a cross. The permanent landing is a refuge from the lanes, not a switch that disables them.
design.mastery: Connect all five foundations and clear without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A completed central connection stays usable through a crossing pair of attacks.
design.routeDecision: Complete a north-south spine or an east-west link first when both a row and a column can lock?

design.captureConsequence: Connecting an island shortens later returns without clearing its occupied district. The permanent center lane never erodes; earned approaches can.
design.counterplay: Use the center spine to switch districts when pressure builds. Walls never close cuts; the islands do. Read both field anchors before a large slice.
design.lesson: Each district contains an eroder and a keeper. A cut between occupied pockets secures only its line; choose the return that improves your next enclosure.
design.mastery: Close a cut in each district and neutralize the eastern hazard without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A modest island connection becomes a new departure around a baffle while the far pocket remains visibly occupied.
design.routeDecision: Bank the short western island return, work around the eastern baffle to reach its taller landing, or risk a broad outer enclosure?

design.captureConsequence: An inner landing shortens a later cut without banking against a wall. Outer returns introduce reclaimed-ground pressure, and two retainers keep each chamber contested until deliberately enclosed.
design.counterplay: The top and bottom baffle ends stay open. Watch both local keepers before crossing; after waking a roamer, turn onto a different return rather than waiting on its new rail. Either partner may travel around the divider to help. Coordinate the Interceptor around exposed lines and the Disruptor around moving threats; neither pulse substitutes for the other.
design.lesson: Interceptor Support removes nearby travelling impacts while Disruptor Support slows nearby enemies. Rescue remains available to both players.
design.mastery: Activate both roamers, with each craft closing in its starting chamber and no knockdowns.
design.memorableMoment: A quick outside escape and a protected inner receiver become two different ways to reopen the same depot.
design.routeDecision: Wake the outer return patrols for quick perimeter access, or wrap the inner baffles to establish receiver landings first?

design.captureConsequence: The near relay opens a permanent non-scoring home dock. Other captures neutralize field only where no keeper remains, and can wake the roamer on reclaimed ground. Captured objectives persist through ordinary recovery.
design.counterplay: Watch both keeper positions before departing; an enemy on each side can leave a line-only capture. Keep an upper or dock return ready before enclosing the ground roamer. The freeze pickup is optional.
design.lesson: The finale combines the familiar enemy-retained capture rule with relay returns and reclaimed-ground pressure. There is no boss shield or release window: enclose the four visible signal objectives and reach the coverage target.
design.mastery: Connect and visit a western wing and either far-eastern platform before clearing without a life loss.
design.memorableMoment: An opened dock can offer a homeward return after a wide reveal wakes the roamer; choose a return rather than wait for a boss opening.
design.routeDecision: Capture the near relay to open the home dock, or establish a far-wing return while the two field keepers occupy different approaches?

design.captureConsequence: Closure cancels the committed attack. The adapted actor still retains its occupied field region, while the existing wall, foundation and patrol rules remain unchanged.
design.counterplay: Prepare a work-pad return before entering the trace, turn only after the visible lock, and avoid following the outer patrol into the narrow approach.
design.lesson: Component-like walls make the alternate heading useful counterplay; the committed target never follows a later turn.
design.mastery: Close on both interior work pads after separate warning locks.
design.memorableMoment: The longer circuit aisle becomes the safe route once the interceptor commits to the obvious line.
design.routeDecision: Take the obvious straight trace, or provoke a lock and switch to the offset aisle through a broad work pad?

design.captureConsequence: A mouth closure may secure only the connecting line; an outside enclosure can instead move patrol pressure.
design.counterplay: Use the broad ring as a return; compare the inner keeper, lower approach keeper and outer contour before crossing.
design.lesson: Closing a ring does not fill an occupied center. The keeper, not the visible loop, determines retained field.
design.mastery: Earn a closure through the ring mouth and connect the ring to the perimeter without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A visually closed ring can still contain unclaimed ground, with its retaining enemy plainly visible.
design.routeDecision: Close the mouth around the inner keeper first, or grow an outside return while the ring remains open?

design.captureConsequence: An outer connection creates new launch angles but cannot claim the occupied courtyard. An inward capture creates shorter interior returns without clearing the outside for free.
design.counterplay: Watch the keeper in the field you are entering. Move along reclaimed ring ground to shorten the exposed route, and close before a keeper reaches your line.
design.lesson: The ring separates two keeper-held fields. Its outer edge offers short returns; its inner edge supports larger enclosures. Both fields matter to the clear.
design.mastery: Complete an inward cut and an outward cut.
design.memorableMoment: A short outer bridge changes the next launch, then an inward enclosure reveals the courtyard at a different scale.
design.routeDecision: Take the short outer bridge first, or move along the ring to choose an inward enclosure?

design.captureConsequence: Join the off-centre shelf to shorten later closures without changing enemy speed tiers.
design.counterplay: The direct departure avoids acceleration; the optional pickup has a broad straight approach.
design.lesson: Speed is a contact bonus with an expiry, not different handling assigned to this level.
design.mastery: Connect the shelf and central landing without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The same long rail becomes an optional launch route, not a compulsory sprint.
design.routeDecision: Use the central return immediately, or detour along a broad rail for an optional speed window?

design.captureConsequence: Closure cancels the committed attack. Field-retaining enemies still determine which regions remain unclaimed, and the existing terrain or patrol consequences remain active.
design.counterplay: Prepare a second return before entering the field. Turn after the target locks, keep the exposed segment short, and let closure cancel the finite commitment.
design.lesson: The interceptor warns and predicts only the observed heading. Its committed target does not follow a later turn.
design.mastery: Neutralize both lethal crossbars and close a cut with an active impact without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A deliberate turn leaves the interceptor travelling toward an empty point while the captured band becomes a safer approach.
design.routeDecision: Keep the obvious crossing after the interceptor locks your heading, or turn toward the central return and neutralize a different hazardous band?

design.captureConsequence: A newly connected work mat extends both your return network and the roamer movement domain.
design.counterplay: Keep a parallel aisle and choose the next departure before the sleeper becomes active.
design.lesson: Opening the board can activate a new threat on reclaimed ground; the warning gives time to leave.
design.mastery: Use three different work mats after waking the roamer.
design.memorableMoment: The best new shortcut becomes a shared route with a visibly awakening threat.
design.routeDecision: Reclaim the middle aisle now and wake its roamer, or join an outer work mat first to preserve another escape?

design.captureConsequence: Connecting two bays can make one useful return network while the remaining bay stays a separate route choice.
design.counterplay: Every mouth is broad; use outside routes instead of following a patrol through a narrow return.
design.lesson: An open mouth is unclaimed field, not a safe doorway. Closing it changes both retention and contour connections.
design.mastery: Connect all three bay foundations without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: Three interrupted contours can be joined in different orders without clearing five repetitive boxes.
design.routeDecision: Bridge the nearby bays for several returns, or approach the distant bay before its frontier patrol arrives?

design.captureConsequence: The growing cross offers shorter return paths; both stationary anchors continue to retain their own regions.
design.counterplay: Choose one short connection at a time. Close before the simultaneous attacks instead of trying to outrun both with a long live trail.
design.lesson: Two known emitters mark a cross. The permanent landing is a refuge from the lanes, not a switch that disables them.
design.mastery: Connect all five foundations and clear without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A completed central connection stays usable through a crossing pair of attacks.
design.routeDecision: Complete a north-south spine or an east-west link first when both a row and a column can lock?

design.captureConsequence: Closing the pocket can separate keeper regions and reshape patrol pressure at the mouth.
design.counterplay: The mouth stays broad enough for a direct route without collecting the freeze pickup.
design.lesson: Combine distinct outer and frontier patrol routes; the optional freeze never replaces a legal return.
design.mastery: Use an inward and an outward return without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: An open shelter becomes two differently threatened approaches after closure.
design.routeDecision: Close the pocket mouth first or cross outward while the frontier patrol works around the other side?

design.captureConsequence: Connection order changes frontier pressure; only the two field keepers retain regions.
design.counterplay: Keep an interior retreat while choosing which optional bonus detour is worth its exposure.
design.lesson: Combine known keeper, outer-patrol and frontier-patrol rules; no new mandatory mechanic.
design.mastery: Connect all three foundations without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The same new bridge is a useful return and a possible future patrol edge.
design.routeDecision: Link the nearer spine first or approach the far island before its frontier patrol comes around?

design.captureConsequence: Each connection changes the next usable return and the patrol contour.
design.counterplay: Use the clear sides of the rungs and observe the frontier before returning. The slow lower approach is optional, not a forced precision sprint.
design.lesson: A sequence of deliberate returns can reduce impact exposure more than a single ambitious crossing.
design.mastery: Connect all three foundations and close a cut with an active impact without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The ladder acquires a new rung through the player’s own capture.
design.routeDecision: Build short diagonal connections between staggered landings, or expose a longer trail to reclaim a larger side?

design.captureConsequence: Connecting one landing leaves the other branch intact, so the next enclosure begins from a materially different angle.
design.counterplay: Read both keepers from the boundary. The near landing limits exposure; the central landing gives more return directions but needs a longer opening cut.
design.lesson: Five disconnected landings turn the early foundation lesson into a real route fork without adding a new rule.
design.mastery: Use both the near-spikelet and central-sun approaches without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: An original sun-and-spikelet spatial rhythm opens into visibly different upper and lower chains.
design.routeDecision: Use the near seed landing to build a short spikelet chain, or bypass it for the broader central sun landing before choosing an upper or lower return?

design.captureConsequence: Enclosing the band neutralizes its slowing effect and creates a faster future approach.
design.counterplay: The first crossing leads to a broad return; inspect the keeper before choosing the exposed shortcut.
design.lesson: Paired dashes slow the craft only while this ground is unclaimed. Enemies keep their catalog speed.
design.mastery: Neutralize the whole slow band without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A route that was slow becomes ordinary reclaimed ground after the enclosure.
design.routeDecision: Cross the short slow band to reach the island, or take the longer clear approach around it?

design.captureConsequence: Enclosing the roamer changes reclaimed-ground pressure; the keepers retain field normally.
design.counterplay: Keep broad cross-connections available. A permanent landing closes the cut but does not protect against an active roamer.
design.lesson: A capture can remove terrain danger and wake a different movement-domain threat at the same time.
design.mastery: Neutralize both lethal banks and close a cut after the roamer activates without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A blocked-looking approach becomes clear, then requires a different return plan as the roamer wakes.
design.routeDecision: Open the northern clear channel or the southern island connection while preserving room for the reclaimed-ground roamer?

design.captureConsequence: Each shore connection offers a shorter next approach around a different breakwater end.
design.counterplay: Keep a second internal landing within reach instead of relying on a single outside-border return.
design.lesson: Shore platforms are real returns; staggered breakwaters and keepers in separated approaches make crossing order matter.
design.mastery: Connect landings on both shores before the final enclosure.
design.memorableMoment: A narrow bridge opens a wide choice of later river crossings.
design.routeDecision: Link the central landing to pass the staggered breakwater, or take the wider outer crossing?

design.captureConsequence: Capturing the inner aisle creates a useful return beside, not on, the obstructing trace.
design.counterplay: The broad work pads provide independent returns; do not chase the outside patrol through a narrow approach.
design.lesson: Component-like walls redirect routes without changing craft speed or controls.
design.mastery: Close from each of the two interior work pads.
design.memorableMoment: A frustrating detour becomes the shorter route once adjacent field is reclaimed.
design.routeDecision: Thread the offset circuit corridor, or accept a longer exposed cut around a trace end?

design.captureConsequence: Join the off-centre shelf to shorten later closures without changing enemy speed tiers.
design.counterplay: The direct departure avoids acceleration; the optional pickup has a broad straight approach.
design.lesson: Speed is a contact bonus with an expiry, not different handling assigned to this level.
design.mastery: Connect the shelf and central landing without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The same long rail becomes an optional launch route, not a compulsory sprint.
design.routeDecision: Use the central return immediately, or detour along a broad rail for an optional speed window?

design.captureConsequence: Capturing the hot pocket creates usable ground; untouched slow ground still delays the craft, never the emitter clock.
design.counterplay: Plan the bend before departure and use the central platform as a fallback when the locked row crosses your trail.
design.lesson: A rail is a return surface, not a wall. Staggered rails change crossing length without changing attack timing.
design.mastery: Join all three foundations and neutralize the lethal pocket without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: One new connector turns offset rails into a useful stepped return.
design.routeDecision: Connect the nearer staggered rail or claim a hazardous pocket first to open the wider side approach?

design.captureConsequence: Closure cancels the committed attack. Field-retaining enemies still determine which regions remain unclaimed, and the existing terrain or patrol consequences remain active.
design.counterplay: Keep the next rung visible, wait for the aim point to lock, then turn toward another landing instead of outrunning the interceptor in a straight line.
design.lesson: Successive changes of heading beat prediction, but each landing also changes the frontier patrol route.
design.mastery: Connect all three foundations and close a cut with an active impact without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A new rung becomes both the next feint and a permanent return while the committed attack passes behind it.
design.routeDecision: Climb through short staggered returns and turn after each lock, or expose one longer route while the frontier patrol controls the next rung?

design.captureConsequence: Two independently earned connectors turn three landings into a usable cross-board return.
design.counterplay: Choose a visible return before entering the upper field and watch the frontier at the far landing.
design.lesson: Each number is a separate capture link. Opening one connector does not open every gate.
design.mastery: Open the eastern connector before the western connector and clear without a life loss.
design.memorableMoment: The same upper trigger can be approached from the outer rail or the newly connected middle platform.
design.routeDecision: Open the nearer link to gain a central launch point, or approach the eastern trigger from the outer boundary first?

design.captureConsequence: The short western connection wakes a non-retaining roamer; broader enclosures expand its reclaimed movement domain. The central landing offers a different next return.
design.counterplay: The tracked body marks the western outside route. Prepare another exit, turn along the perimeter after banking, or have your partner connect the middle landing before you return through the changed ground. Baffles are walls, never returns.
design.lesson: A quick return can become a shared patrol route. The full one-second wake warning gives time to choose a fresh departure.
design.mastery: Activate the roamer before clearing, with a closure from each craft and no knockdowns.
design.memorableMoment: The line that rescued one craft becomes a moving threat while a partner opens a second approach.
design.routeDecision: Take the short outside return and wake its roamer, or connect toward the middle landing before opening that escape?

design.captureConsequence: The two relay captures assemble a cross-board reclaimed route without changing any chamber keeper’s domain.
design.counterplay: Use different launch heights around the central spine; avoid treating four chambers as four compulsory identical cuts.
design.lesson: Each occupied chamber remains a separate field problem. A junction opens traversal, not an automatic chamber clear.
design.mastery: Use both opened junctions and clear all required objectives without a life loss.
design.memorableMoment: A formerly blocked side of the central hub becomes a useful return from either adjacent chamber.
design.routeDecision: Use the first opened junction to move through the hub or work around the outside to reach the opposite relay before the frontier approaches?

design.captureConsequence: The first bridge creates a new approach angle, but foundations still earn no score.
design.counterplay: Watch each keeper before departing; close early when its path threatens the line.
design.lesson: An interior spawn offers several departures; reaching the perimeter is a route choice.
design.mastery: Reach two different perimeter sides.
design.memorableMoment: A tiny starting island becomes the centre of a growing network.
design.routeDecision: Connect to the near western rail or commit to a longer eastern return?

design.captureConsequence: A capture beside the bend changes the next frontier without changing the permanent return or denominator.
design.counterplay: Use the wide central bend to change approach, and neutralize the optional slow patch before a longer crossing.
design.lesson: A connected foundation can separate occupied field regions while frontier and perimeter patrols keep distinct routes.
design.mastery: Earn territory on both sides of the dogleg and neutralize the slow patch without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A route that looks long on the board can be the shorter exposed trail.
design.routeDecision: Enclose beside the short bend, or use the long dogleg to leave the patrol on the opposite side?

design.captureConsequence: An approach capture creates useful return ground without automatically defeating the core. The same exposed-stage release rule applies.
design.counterplay: The walls block turns and never close cuts. The frontier follows your new return edge; the roamer activates on reclaimed ground.
design.lesson: Deep receiver galleries share the Sentinel field. Choose returns outside the baffles before committing to an inner cut.
design.mastery: Capture the lower receiver before the upper receiver, in separate closures, and clear without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The second receiver approach becomes visible beyond the first gallery wall.
design.routeDecision: Secure the upper gallery approach first, or the lower landing, before turning around a receiver baffle?

design.captureConsequence: The opened yards share return ground while their outer field remains governed by the ordinary enemy-retained fill rule.
design.counterplay: Leave a long escape corridor before reclaiming the roamer and use the upper landing as an alternate departure.
design.lesson: An opened connector is permanent, but reclaimed-ground roamers may still use it after activation.
design.mastery: Visit both outer yards after opening their links and clear without a life loss.
design.memorableMoment: A new cross-yard connection becomes both an escape route and possible roamer territory.
design.routeDecision: Connect the western yard first or claim the eastern trigger while keeping a retreat away from the dormant roamer?

design.captureConsequence: Neutralizing terrain and protecting a return connection solve different parts of the same route.
design.counterplay: Keep the middle reserve and choose an approach outside the active roamer’s reclaimed domain.
design.lesson: Capture order should make the next route easier, not demand that every repeated cluster be cleared.
design.mastery: Neutralize both marked terrain areas and capture both anchors without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: An awkward stagger becomes a useful diagonal sequence of axis-aligned captures.
design.routeDecision: Secure the slowing northern connection first, or enclose the southern danger pocket before banking its anchor?

design.captureConsequence: Every bridge creates a new possible closure; no route requires a lucky bonus.
design.counterplay: Watch each keeper before departing; close early when its path threatens the line.
design.lesson: Choose a route using both return distance and the future shape of retained regions.
design.mastery: Join the two side outposts without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The final bridge turns separated outposts into a useful loop.
design.routeDecision: Use a top or bottom stepping platform, or attempt the exposed direct bridge?

design.captureConsequence: Capturing either anchor both protects its cell and opens a non-scoring connector. Earned side shortcuts remain vulnerable to warned erosion.
design.counterplay: Keep the live route short: both the keeper and eroder send visible fronts when they strike an unfinished trail, while direct body contact remains immediate. Use the broad center corridor to change your approach.
design.lesson: A territory repair and a trail-impact closure race are familiar but different decisions. Permanent foundations, opened connectors and captured objective anchors protect the planned return.
design.mastery: Traverse both opened connectors before clearing without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: An opened T-shaped return stays intact while a nearby earned edge is reopened.
design.routeDecision: Open the upper protected link first, or invest in the lower anchor while the keeper and eroder occupy different corridors?

design.captureConsequence: An enclosure can activate a rover on newly reclaimed ground. Preserve more than one exit instead of treating a large fill as permanent safety.
design.counterplay: The optional speed anchors sit on broad straight approaches. Choose the upper or lower platform before waking a rover; the late reserve is expendable, never a completion key.
design.lesson: Speed belongs to its collector; enemy pressure and reclaimed return routes remain a shared responsibility.
design.mastery: Take a timed pickup while your partner is cutting, activate both roamers, and clear with returns from both pilots and no knockdowns.
design.memorableMoment: The fast pilot establishes a long outside connection while the partner keeps clear of the first tracked body waking inside the depot.
design.routeDecision: Use a speed detour for an outside return while the partner shapes an escape from a waking rover, or keep normal handling and connect the bays first?

design.captureConsequence: The two occupied chambers retain independently. One partner can finish a material job while the other builds the shared coverage.
design.counterplay: The west orchard must be enclosed, never crossed unclaimed. The east orchard is crossable but prolongs exposure; the divider is a wall, not a return.
design.lesson: Equal controls do not mean identical jobs: lethal and slow field call for different approaches.
design.mastery: Neutralize both orchards, with each craft closing in its starting chamber and no knockdowns.
design.memorableMoment: Different material problems resolve into two connected, ordinary movement areas.
design.routeDecision: Enclose the lethal orchard from outside while the other craft crosses the slow bay, or swap roles around the perimeter?

design.captureConsequence: Capturing beside a square wall creates an earned shortcut along that side; the wall itself never closes a trail.
design.counterplay: Choose a pad beyond one opening before leaving. The second window’s exit is lower, so reassess keeper positions instead of repeating the first crossing.
design.lesson: The offset cutwork shapes are walls, not circuit paths or safe ground. Their open mouths preserve ordinary enemy-retained field connectivity.
design.mastery: Close once through a square window and once around a closed end while visiting both interior pads.
design.memorableMoment: A reclaimed edge beside the first component window turns an awkward second-window approach into a short return.
design.routeDecision: Thread the staggered square openings toward an interior work pad, or wrap a closed component-window end and earn a wider outside return?

design.captureConsequence: A connection makes a new return surface, not a guaranteed large reveal. The next enclosure depends on which side each keeper occupies.
design.counterplay: Read the western keeper before enclosing the near shore and the eastern keeper before the long crossing. Reposition on the island to choose an upper or lower departure.
design.lesson: An interior outpost offers several departures. Keepers on opposite sides can retain both regions after a cut; a small bridge can still create useful return angles.
design.mastery: Reach two different perimeter sides.
design.memorableMoment: A line-only bridge becomes the launch point for a smaller enclosure around the keeper on that shore.
design.routeDecision: Establish the short western bridge beside its keeper, or time the longer eastern return before choosing the next enclosure?

design.captureConsequence: An upper closure creates a compact return near the inside keeper; a lower closure preserves a longer outside line toward the bonus.
design.counterplay: Reposition on the safe pocket spine, watch the inside keeper, then commit from the upper or lower mouth; neither route is a single-exit trap.
design.lesson: Alternating foundation bands and negative-space mouths redirect travel without introducing a rule ahead of its taught campaign arc.
design.mastery: Close once from each band mouth and collect the existing freeze bonus without a loss.
design.memorableMoment: A stepped geometric band becomes two readable pocket mouths with different return value.
design.routeDecision: Leave the pocket through the upper woven band for a short keeper read, or stage on the lower band before sweeping toward the freeze bonus?

design.captureConsequence: A large capture removes field danger but can start a new reclaimed-ground threat for both craft.
design.counterplay: Make a second exit before enclosing the tracked body. Move away during WAKING; an active roamer reflects rather than chasing either partner.
design.lesson: A dormant roamer does not keep territory unclaimed. Reclaim its full body and the one-second warning precedes danger on reclaimed ground.
design.mastery: Activate the roamer before clearing, with a closure from each craft and no knockdowns.
design.memorableMoment: The still tracked body wakes inside territory that both craft just earned.
